chapter_seo_title: Dung-Beetle Ascension Explained — Li Huowang Becomes the Great Elder (Dao-Twisted Ch.405)
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang discovers three Dung-Beetle Ascensions have made him the Ao-Jing Sect’s Great Elder—able to channel Bashe without the Thousand Greats Record. But every step closer to the god is a step into worse trouble.
og_description: Li Huowang learns he no longer needs the Thousand Greats Record to sacrifice to Bashe. That’s not a power-up. That’s the god touching him directly.
twitter_title: Li Huowang just got a promotion he really, really didn’t want
twitter_description: The Ao-Jing sect recognizes him as Great Elder after three Dung-Beetle Ascensions. His reward: offering his own flesh directly, no book needed.

lore_anchors.definition: A ritual that trades excruciating, dual-layer pain for power from Bashe, named after the dung beetle’s filth-to-life transformation. Completing three makes one a Great Elder.
A red bamboo slip containing the Ao-Jing Sect’s sacrifice techniques; its rituals channel Bashe by inflicting extreme agony on the user.
The highest openly acknowledged rank in the Ao-Jing Sect, reached after three Dung-Beetle Ascensions; previously thought to be a title exclusively used by Zuowandao impostors.
The highest-ranked inner circle of the Zuowandao; their appearance signals an escalation in the enemy’s threat level.
A fictional sect fusing Zoroastrianism and Nestorian Christianity; original owners of the *Thousand Greats Record* and devoted worshippers of Bashe.
A primordial, pain-feeding god worshipped by the Ao-Jing Sect; it can only be perceived by merging the five senses into a single new awareness.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What exactly changed when Li Huowang completed three Dung-Beetle Ascensions?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The *Thousand Greats Record* was previously required as an intermediary to channel Bashe's power. After three Ascensions, Li Huowang's flesh itself has become the offering point—he can sacrifice directly without the book.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Does Li Huowang want this power?
cultural_notes_faq.a: No. He recognizes it as a double-edged advantage—it removes his vulnerability to having the *Record* stolen, but it also means he is now physically closer to Bashe, and he has no idea what other transformations the Ascensions have wrought.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is the Zuowandao going silent a bad sign?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Li Huowang correctly deduces that if small-scale attacks fail to harm Zhuge Yuan, the Zuowandao will skip the minions and mobilize their most dangerous assets—likely the Four Joys and North Wind—for a decisive strike.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Was the Great Elder title always real inside the Ao-Jing Sect?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Yes. All the "Great Elders" readers encountered before were Zuowandao impostors, but the rank itself is genuine within the Ao-Jing Sect's hierarchy. Xia Risheng's recognition confirms the title's legitimacy.
